A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All pages, equations, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original ASL sampling experiments, empirical stability distributions and MCMC solution probabilities, including appendix experiments in Figures 4–8.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds binary-perceptron experiments on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR10 in Appendix E.4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 revises the written AMP updates by inserting 1/sqrt(N) and 1/N normalization factors and returns variance as well as mean marginals. The overarching ASL procedure, log-potential and τ-annealing schedule remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates randomly generated perceptron instances. Appendix E.4 adds structured image data: MNIST classes 3/8, FashionMNIST classes 5/7 and CIFAR10 classes 3/8, including Gaussian-projected MNIST and FashionMNIST representations. This substantially extends the evaluated data conditions.

E2.justification: The new structured-data comparisons add temperature-annealed MCMC with a step potential, labeled U(s)=Θ(s). They also report U(s)=-sΘ(s), whereas the retained synthetic comparisons use U(s)=-sΘ(-s); equivalence of these differently signed potentials cannot be assumed.

E3.justification: Appendix E.4 introduces benchmark-specific settings: 100/784 sweeps for unprojected MNIST and FashionMNIST, 1000/3000 for CIFAR10, and N sweeps for projected dimensions 32, 64, 1024 and 2048. Comparators receive matching sweep budgets. Existing synthetic evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The added raw-versus-projected image experiments examine solver behavior under representation changes and varying projection dimension (Figures 9–14). Existing finite-size, sweep-budget and stability-distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figures 9, 12 and 15 explicitly describe error bars as standard deviations estimated over 100 problem instances. v2 already reports averaging 250 ASL simulations and displays MCMC error bars, but lacks this explicit uncertainty description. Retained experiments show no reported increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Figures 9–15 add substantial solving-probability results on structured datasets, generally favoring τ-annealing, especially with larger projected representations. These measure zero-error solution success, not held-out accuracy. Figures 1–8 and the approximately 0.65 ASL and 0.55 τ-annealing thresholds are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2 revises the binary reference-system entropic and energetic expressions. Appendix F.1.2 corrects differentiation from q to its conjugate and restores a missing factor of 1/2. The replica framework, assumptions and limiting-behavior argument otherwise remain intact.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions retain the same scope: replica-based sampling thresholds, spherical-perceptron samplability, the binary log-potential sampler and τ-annealed MCMC. The new experiments support the existing structured-data applicability claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly identifies ASL samples with dense clusters and interprets τ-annealing's ability to travel far through solution space as support for targeting a large dense cluster. The existing limitations concerning AMP on structured data and replica-symmetric analysis remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E.4 supplies new reproduction details, including selected classes, binary labels, feature dimensions, Gaussian projection-matrix generation, temperatures and sweep budgets. Moving existing AMP implementation details from Section 4.2 to Appendix A does not constitute new disclosure.

R1.justification: v3 adds energy-based-model and Bayesian context references, dataset citations and a comparison with Budzynski et al.'s k-NAESAT reweighting approach. It also replaces the cited stochastic-interpolant work. The central positioning relative to earlier sampling and perceptron research remains stable.

P1.justification: The introduction and replica-method explanation receive targeted expansions and rewriting. AMP channel definitions move from Section 4.2 to Appendix A, and Appendix E.4 is integrated into the narrative. The overall section structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figures 9–15 add a substantial suite of comparative displays covering image datasets, projections and sweep budgets. Figures 1–8 are retained, while Algorithm 1 is reformatted and several existing elements shift position.

improvement.justification: Appendix E.4 supplies empirical support for structured-data applicability that v2 asserted without testing, while equation corrections improve technical accuracy. These are useful gains, although the new solving-success results do not establish sampling fairness, and the differing baseline-potential signs remain unexplained. The central theory and original evidence are largely unchanged.
